title: Lower Wing Cover Panel External Repair Patch at the Leading Edge Access Bay
abstract: External repair patch on the lower shell of the wing at the leading edge access bay, for impact and puncture damage from ground equipment, with the fuel tank sealing requirement.

sections.purpose: Permanent external repair patch for impact or puncture damage in the lower wing cover panel adjacent to the leading edge access bay, including the fuel tank sealing requirement where the damage is inside the tank boundary.
sections.damage_assessment: The damage is almost always caused by ground equipment during a leading edge access, and it is found on the lower shell within reach of a work platform. The assessment must first establish whether the damaged area is inside the fuel tank boundary, because the sealing requirement and the approval route both change if it is. The panel thickness must be measured around the damage, and the extent of any delamination or disbond established by ultrasonic. Damage that has deformed the panel rather than only removing material is outside this scheme. The proximity to the access bay cut-out must be checked; a patch that overlaps the cut-out edge changes the load path around the bay and requires a different repair.
sections.repair_procedure: Defuel and purge the tank where the damage is inside the tank boundary, and observe the tank entry precautions. Remove the protective treatment and the sealant from the repair area. Establish the extent of the damage by ultrasonic. Machine out the damaged material to the shape given on repair drawing RD-57-10-12-004, keeping the corner radii above the stated minimum. Prepare the patch landing area. Position the external patch using the shear tie stock D5710120643308 as the patch blank, with the doubler D5710127013579 under the leading edge, as shown on the drawing. Drill the fastener pattern and install the fasteners AGS17834-4B wet, using the closing item D5710127178146 at the outboard edge. Where the repair is inside the tank boundary, apply the interior tank sealant to the full fastener pattern and the patch periphery, and do the sealant cure and inspection before the tank is closed. Restore the exterior protective treatment and apply the aerodynamic fillet.
sections.inspection_requirements: Ultrasonic inspection of the machined area before the patch is fitted and of the patch periphery after installation. Where the repair is inside the tank boundary, a fuel leak check is required after refuelling and again after the first flight. A repeat ultrasonic inspection of the patch periphery is required every 6 000 flight hours. The aerodynamic fillet is inspected at every A-check for loss of adhesion, because a lifted fillet at this station collects water and initiates corrosion under the patch edge.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Damage up to 80 mm in any direction, not deforming the panel, and not closer than 40 mm to the leading edge access bay cut-out edge.

repair_drawings.title: External repair patch, lower wing cover panel

materials.description: SHEAR TIE STOCK, USED AS PATCH BLANK

type_data.fastener_pattern: Three rows, 56 fasteners, 24 mm pitch, 18 mm edge distance, corner radii not less than 12 mm
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Not life limited. Repeat ultrasonic inspection of the patch periphery every 6 000 flight hours, and a fuel leak check where the repair is inside the tank boundary.
